neighbours.label: air or wind moving through a system of fans, vents, compressors or ducts, as opposed to the same frames about vehicles and rooms, and to other machines
fire: Large exhaust fans push stale air through the ducts.
Open the valve and let the air bleed from the compressor tank.
These attic vents need no power and are driven by wind.
Warm air rises up the shaft and leaves through the roof.
A blower forces cold air across the coils.
Passive ventilation draws outside air through the crawl space.
The turbine draws air through the intake at high speed.
Dust clogs the filter and slows airflow to the bedrooms.
quiet: Large farm trucks push heavy loads through the mud.
Open the gate and let the sheep out from the holding pen.
These garden lamps need no wires and are charged by sunlight.
Warm bread sits on the shelf and sells before the noon rush.
A clerk stamps cold cash forms across the desk.
Regular practice builds young players through the long season.
The bus carries kids through the town at low speed.
Grease clogs the sink and slows dishes in the kitchen.

short: air through vents, fans and compressors
notes: Card and probes also fire on channel biology ('conductance' 1.07), which this does not cover; 'potassium channel' scored only 0.01.
